notes:
Account summary: Saffron is a regional telco support org (consumer + SMB) looking to replace brittle macros and improve agent TTR with an assistant. Primary interest: reliable RAG over heterogeneous KBs (Zendesk, Confluence, S3 logs, product release notes), strong citation + freshness controls, and deterministic tool-calling for IMAP/CRM updates.

Key requirements / constraints:
- Workload: live agent assist (primary), ticket summarization (post-call), and outbound guidance (auto-drafts). Also reranking for suggested KB articles.
- Latency targets: p50 < 150ms for vector lookup + model response under normal load; p99 budget <= 600ms. Hard SLA during spikes (holiday/launch): sustain ~1.2k concurrent interactions with graceful degradation.
- Throughput: baseline ~250 qps, peaks up to 1k+ qps during incidents. Cost sensitivity: moderate — will trade some cost for reliability.
- Retrieval: need multi-source retriever with source-aware citations, freshness window (configurable per source), and provenance returned to agents. Support for hybrid retrieval (sparse + dense) desirable.
- Safety/quality: evaluate for hallucination rate on 5k labeled tickets; must hit >= 95% citation precision for suggested KB passages.
- Security/compliance: VPC deployment preferred; KMS integration required; SOC2 + SSO/SAML mandatory; data residency options for EU customers.

POC success metrics (customer):
- Citation precision >= 95% (measured on 500-sample eval set).
- Agent time-to-resolution (TTR) drop >= 20% in simulated runs.
- P99 latency <= 600ms at 1k concurrent interactions (dedicated config).
- Tool-calls executed reliably with idempotency and audit logs.

Technical notes / SE playbook items:
- Ingest plan: incremental sync from Zendesk (delta tokens), Confluence full snapshot, S3 raw logs for transcripts. Need pipeline for freshness TTL per-source.
- Retrieval architecture: test out vector DB + tagging for source priority; try prefix caching for frequent intents. Evaluate Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching under spikes.
- Fallbacks: policy to route to smaller quantized model for low-priority queries during extreme load, but keep agent assist pinned to higher-quality variant.
- Observability: customer needs per-route token-level cost, citation hit-rate dashboards, and rollback hooks for bad rollouts.
